chapter.li: LEChapter61 Verse1 Soon after Moroni had sent his letter to the chief governor, he received a letter from Parhoron the chief governor. This is what it said: VerseEnd Verse2 I Parhoron, the chief governor of this land, send this to Moroni, the chief captain over the army. I tell 2PSF you, Moroni, I have no pleasure in 2PSF your great difficulties; they distress me. VerseEnd Verse3 But there are some who are pleased by 2PSF your troubles. There is a rebellion underway against me and against all the freemen. Our opponents are very numerous. VerseEnd Verse4 They have attempted to remove me from the judgment seat, and have caused all of the resulting difficulties by their iniquity. Their rhetoric and deceit have confused and misled many people to sympathize with them, resulting in our many difficulties. They have interfered with resupplying 2PSF you, and have intimidated our freemen so that they haven’t joined 2PSF you. VerseEnd Verse5 I’ve been exiled and have fled to Gideon with as many men as I could. VerseEnd Verse6 From here I’ve sent a proclamation throughout this part of the land. People are flocking to us daily, with their weapons, in defense of their country and their freedom and to pay back our wrongs. VerseEnd Verse7 Indeed, so many have joined us that those insurrectionists now face stiff resistance; they’re now afraid of us and don’t dare start the battle against us. VerseEnd Verse8 But they control the city of Zarahemla, and they have appointed a king to now rule. He has written to the Lamanite king and made an alliance with him. As part of their alliance, he has agreed to hold and defend the city of Zarahemla, expecting that will enable the Lamanites to conquer the rest of the land. He anticipates he will be appointed king over this people after they’re conquered by the Lamanites. VerseEnd

Verse9 Now in 2PSF your letter 2PSF you have criticized and judged me, but it doesn’t matter. I’m not angry, but am pleased by 2PSF your patriotic heart. I don’t seek power, only to retain my judgment seat to protect my people’s rights and liberty. I stand firmly in the liberty that God has given us. VerseEnd

Verse10 Now we will oppose wickedness, even to the death. We wouldn’t kill the Lamanites if they would stay in their own land. VerseEnd Verse11 We wouldn’t kill our fellow Nephites if they didn’t rise up in rebellion and lift their sword against us. VerseEnd Verse12 We would submit to the burden of slavery if God’s justice demanded it, or if He commanded us to do so. VerseEnd Verse13 But He doesn’t command us to put ourselves under the control of our enemies, but to put our trust in Him and He’ll rescue us. VerseEnd Verse14 Therefore my dear brother Moroni, let us resist evil. And any evil we can’t resist with our words, including rebellions and defections, let us resist with our swords, to preserve our freedom, so we can have joy worshiping in our congregation and obeying our Redeemer and our God. VerseEnd Verse15 Therefore come quickly to join me with a few of 2PSF your men, and leave the rest in Lehi and Teancum’s charge. Give them orders to follow God’s Spirit in conducting the war in that part of the land, for that’s the very spirit of freedom within them. VerseEnd Verse16 I’ve sent a few provisions to them, to feed them while 2PSF you come to aid me. VerseEnd Verse17 Recruit any force 2PSF you can while on 2PSF your march here; and we’ll immediately go against those defectors in God’s strength, directed by the faith we share. VerseEnd Verse18 We’ll take Zarahemla, get control of provisions, and then relieve Lehi and Teancum. We’ll strike them with the Lord’s strength, and put an end to this sinful rebellion. VerseEnd

Verse19 2PSF Your letter made me rejoice, Moroni. Because I was a little worried about what to do, whether it was right for us to attack fellow Nephites. VerseEnd Verse20 However, as 2PSF you said: Unless they repent, the Lord has commanded 2PSF you to go against them. VerseEnd Verse21 See that 2PSF you bless Lehi and Teancum in the Lord. Tell them not to be afraid, since God will protect them, and all those who stand firmly in the liberty God has given us. Now I end my letter to my dear brother Moroni. VerseEnd
